scope: Release regression measurements on already exposed frozen suites, not new sealed evaluation or model selection

runtime.backend: llama.cpp CPU via public ctypes bridge
runtime.model_identity_note: The loaded benchmark process retained the previous configuration-fingerprint API name. The final package uses the GGUF-file fingerprint instead; only metadata changed, not model bytes or arithmetic.

execution: Sequential POST /v1/systemone on a separate loopback port. No retries, truncation, prompt tuning, calibration, or failed-case exclusions. Targets excluded from requests; scoring is external. Each error counts incorrect against the full population.
timing_scope: Descriptive request wall times only, not a controlled latency benchmark; shared desktop, concurrent low-priority build/render/acceptance checks

sciq.rendering: Original test question, empty context, no support passage. Original frozen option order from Random(SHA256(seed:index:question)), seed20260924; letter labels A-D.
sciq.metric: Argmax exact-choice accuracy; all official test rows; no exclusions
sciq.rights: CC-BY-NC-3.0 according to dataset card. Used for local noncommercial evaluation only. Dataset input text is not redistributed in result ledgers.

decision_panel.metric: Choice/Score argmax exact class; Noul threshold0.5. Native Score independently reads each criterion before normalization.
decision_panel.exposure: Source families were used in training; panel was previously consumed for final evaluation and comparisons.

jevbench.implementation: Archived upstream TypeSafeAdapter.build_request and score_task, including lexicographic argmax ties and distribution validation; no upstream runner retries
jevbench.exposure: Public tasks only; no sealed result, composite ranking, or paid comparator call

nimble_public.input_policy: Every reconstructed subset must hash-match the author's frozen subset manifest; original JSON preserved
nimble_public.metric: Existing local assess() exact-label argmax scoring; native Score, unlike Nimble's enum/Choice rating mode

publication: Raw ledgers retain request hashes, row IDs, model responses, metrics, and timing; benchmark input text is omitted. Comparator numbers are explicitly historical local NF4 or author-published, never new GGUF comparator runs.
